shareErrors.notAShareFile: That file is not a Diff Bro shared diff.
shareErrors.notForYou: This shared diff is sealed for a different machine — it can only be opened by its addressed recipient.
shareErrors.tampered: Rejected: the file was modified in transit (or is corrupted) — decryption failed.
shareErrors.unknownSigner: Sealed correctly, but signed by an unknown sender — add their public key first (File → Add Trusted Key).
shareErrors.badSignature: Signature check failed — the file was modified or corrupted.
shareErrors.badTrustedKey: The stored public key for this sender is unreadable — remove it and add their key file again.
shareErrors.expired: This shared diff has already expired.
shareErrors.invalidTtl: Rejected: shared diffs cannot live longer than a week.
shareErrors.unknownRecipient: Recipient not found among trusted keys.
shareErrors.renamed: This shared diff was renamed — its integrity is tied to its original hashed filename, so it was refused. Ask the sender to re-send it unchanged.
shareErrors.identityUnavailable: Your identity key couldn’t be unlocked (the OS keychain may be locked). Nothing was changed — unlock it and try again.
shareErrors.vaultKeyUnavailable: The saved-diff key couldn’t be unlocked (the OS keychain may be locked). Your saved diffs and snippets are intact — unlock it and try again.
shareErrors.notASnippetFile: That file is not a Diff Bro snippets export.
shareErrors.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase, or the file is corrupted.
shareErrors.corrupted: The file could not be read after decryption.
shareErrors.malformed: That snippets file is not shaped like a valid export and was rejected.
shareErrors.tooLarge: That snippets file exceeds the allowed size limits and was rejected.

compare.title: Two files, any way you like
compare.body: Drop them anywhere on this window, or click a slot to browse. Diff Bro picks the viewer for you — text, JSON tree, spreadsheet grid or diagram.

share.title: Send it sealed, not screenshotted
share.body: Share locks this comparison so only the people you pick can open it, and it stops opening after however long you choose. First time with someone, you swap a small key file: Security ▸ Share My Public Key sends yours, Security ▸ Add Trusted Key takes theirs. After that it is two clicks.

library.title: Your library, narrowing as you type
library.body: Saved diffs, shared diffs and snippets all live here. Watch the list filter as the search fills in.

quick-look.title: The same search, over any app
quick-look.body: Press {shortcut} and this box opens on top of whatever you are working in — even while Diff Bro is minimised. Find a snippet, copy it, press Escape. Try it now.

settings-open.title: The rest is in the menus
settings-open.body: Fourteen themes, size limits, where your data is kept, the shortcut above — all of it is in Settings, at the bottom of the File menu.

settings-panes.title: One pane at a time
settings-panes.body: Everything else is down this list — Shortcuts for the quick look-up chord, Storage for where your data is kept, Limits for how large a file may be.

settings-tips.title: And this is the off switch
settings-tips.body: Tips appear again after an update. Turn them off here — or press Show tour whenever you want this walk-through back.

snippet-new.title: Save commonly used text or code
snippet-new.body: A deploy payload, a prompt, a config block — the + here starts one, and the search finds it again next week.

snippet-save.title: Name it, tag it, save it
snippet-save.body: This one is filled in already. Press the ringed Save to keep it — the sidebar and the quick look-up both find it afterwards. Next moves on either way.

snippet-drag.title: Drag it anywhere in here
snippet-drag.body: The whole comparison area takes a drop — you don’t have to land on a file box. A snippet can face a file, or another snippet.

diagram-open.title: A Mermaid snippet draws itself
diagram-open.body: This one is a diagram — it previews live as you type it. Two versions of one compare as a picture rather than as text.

diagram.title: A diagram change, as a diagram
diagram.body: Here it is: the same flow, one revision apart. Every added, removed or changed node is marked on the picture, so you read the change instead of hunting for it in the text.

why.whitespace: Whitespace only means something in a text comparison

backupSettings.takenAfterASaveNever: Taken after a save, never on a timer — an app left open all day writes nothing.
backupSettings.restoringReplacesYourSnippetsAnd: Restoring replaces your snippets and kept diffs with that copy. Anything saved since is lost.
backupSettings.lastBackup: Last backup {when} ago · {kept} kept · {size} on disk.
backupSettings.restored: Restored {diffs} diffs and {snippets} snippets. Restart Diff Bro to see them.

cliSettings.helpHint: Run {cmd} in a terminal for the long form of any of these.
cliSettings.outOfDate: This command was installed by an older build and needs reinstalling to work.

encryptDecryptDialog.unauthenticatedNote: AES-256-CBC is {word} — a successful decrypt does not prove the data is untampered. For decrypting external payloads only.

dialog.encryptsYourIdentityKeysTrusted: Encrypts your identity keys, trusted hosts, snippets, saved diffs and settings into one passphrase-protected file. Diffs that expire are left out. Keep the passphrase safe — it's the only way to restore.
dialog.restoresIdentityKeysTrustedHosts: Restores identity keys, trusted hosts, snippets, saved diffs and settings from a backup file. Enter the passphrase it was created with. This overwrites your current identity keys.

handoffDialog.optionalGoesInTheMessage: Optional — goes in the message body
handoffDialog.toFromTheirTrustedKeys: To — from their trusted keys, not typed here

settings.subject: Subject

settings.templateHint: {name} and {expires} are filled in from the diff. Your mail app sends the message — Diff Bro opens it and copies the sealed file so you can paste it in.

diffImageDialog.hiddenColumns: About {n} more screen of columns sits off the right edge and isn’t in the picture. Widen the window to take it in. | About {n} more screens of columns sit off the right edge and aren’t in the picture. Widen the window to take them in.
diffImageDialog.truncated: This {noun} was longer than the export height — the picture stops partway down. Raise {setting} in Settings → Limits to capture more.

continueTourDialog.thatIsTheEverydayRoute: That is the everyday route covered. The rest is about keeping your own material in here — saving a snippet, comparing two of them, and previewing a diagram. About a minute.

tourOverlay.notWhileTheTourIs: Not while the tour is running

pasteConfirmDialog.bothSidesAlreadyHaveContent: Both sides already have content. Paste your clipboard into the left side, replacing it? What's there will be lost.
pasteConfirmDialog.pasteYourClipboardIntoThe: Paste your clipboard into the comparison to diff it? It fills the empty side (or starts a paste comparison), and is only read after you confirm.

addTrustedKeyDialog.name: Name
addTrustedKeyDialog.intro: Adding {whose} public key so you can receive diffs they share. The name is prefilled from what they called their key — keep it or rename it. Fingerprint {fp}.
addTrustedKeyDialog.vouch: This key says it replaces {who}, and that key signed the claim. Check the fingerprint with them anyway — anyone holding their old key could have signed it.
addTrustedKeyDialog.fromYourClipboard: Read from your clipboard — check the fingerprint with the sender before adding.

recipientPicker.showOnlyRecipientsWithAn: Show only recipients with an email address
recipientPicker.noneHaveEmail: No trusted key has an email address yet.

removeTrustedKeyDialog.confirm: Remove {name} from your trusted keys? You won't be able to open sealed diffs signed by it, or share to it, until you re-add its {ext}.
removeTrustedKeyDialog.alreadySealed: You have sealed {n} diff for this key. Removing it doesn't reach them — they're already on the other machine, and stay readable until they expire. | You have sealed {n} diffs for this key. Removing it doesn't reach them — they're already on the other machine, and stay readable until they expire.

rotateKeyDialog.aNewKeyTakesOver: A new key takes over from here. Your old one is kept so that diffs already sealed to it still open — it is only ever used to read, never to send.
rotateKeyDialog.doThisIfYourMachine: Do this if your machine or your key may have been exposed.
rotateKeyDialog.doneNote: Your new fingerprint is {fp}. Send your public key again — until each person imports it, anything you seal will reach them as an unknown sender.
rotateKeyDialog.alreadyShared: Diffs you have {shared} stay readable by the people you sent them to. They were sealed with {their} keys; yours only signed them. Replacing a key cannot take anything back.
rotateKeyDialog.retiredKept: {n} earlier key is kept for reading. Destroying it gives up any diff still sealed to it that you have not opened. | {n} earlier keys are kept for reading. Destroying them gives up any diff still sealed to them that you have not opened.
rotateKeyDialog.understandDestroy: I understand, and want the old key destroyed | I understand, and want the old keys destroyed
rotateKeyDialog.destroyOld: Destroy old key | Destroy old keys

diffDialog.nameItAndSendIt: Name it and send it — they import it to receive your diffs.
diffDialog.asSoonAsTheirKey: As soon as their key is added you can pick them as a recipient — this dialog updates automatically.
diffDialog.sealedIntro: Shared diffs are sealed for one recipient, using your public key ({fp}); the private half never leaves this machine.
diffDialog.sealedFor: The file is encrypted so only the chosen recipient can open it, and signed so any modification — including its expiry time — is rejected. | One file only these {n} can open, signed so any modification — including its expiry time — is rejected.
diffDialog.sameExpiry: It expires at the same moment as your local copy.
diffDialog.openTheirKey: Open the {ext} file they sent you.

keyDialog.shownToWhoeverImportsThis: Shown to whoever imports this key, so they recognize it's from you. Not secret, and not part of the key's identity.
keyDialog.intro: This is {your} public key — hand it to the other person so they can receive diffs you share. To receive {their} diffs, use {menu} on the file {they} send you. You never import your own key.
keyDialog.emailItTip: Open your mail app with the key file on the clipboard, ready to paste

trustedKeysDialog.publicKeysOfPeopleYou: Public keys of people you can share sealed diffs with. Give a key an email address to email its diffs from here.
trustedKeysDialog.noKeysYet: No trusted keys yet. Add someone’s {ext} (or drop it onto the window).

diffNotices.couldNotCopyThatAs: Could not copy that as a file.

diffNotices.tooLargeToShareA: Too large to share — a shared diff carries its own copy of both files.
diffNotices.tooLargeToCopyAs: Too large to copy as a patch — that needs both files in full.
diffNotices.tooLargeToExportAn: Too large to export — an HTML export embeds both files.
diffNotices.bothSidesLookLikeStructured: Both sides look like structured data — pretty-print?

diffNotices.copiedAsFile: {name} copied as a file — paste it where you need it.

snippetNotices.signedButNotByAny: Signed, but not by any of your trusted keys — treat these snippets as untrusted.

emailNotices.cancelledNothingWasSealedOr: Cancelled — nothing was sealed or saved.
emailNotices.oneOfThoseRecipientsIs: One of those recipients is no longer a trusted key.
emailNotices.thatAddressCouldNotBe: That address could not be used — check it under Security → Trusted keys.
emailNotices.thatNoteIsTooLong: That note is too long for a mail link — shorten it and try again.
emailNotices.noMailAppIsSet: No mail app is set up to handle links on this machine.
emailNotices.rejectedSharedDiffsCannotLive: Rejected: shared diffs cannot live longer than a week.

imageExportNotices.thisSavedDiffHasExpired: This saved diff has expired or could not be decrypted.
imageExportNotices.couldNotTakeAPicture: Could not take a picture of this diff.
imageExportNotices.hiddenSnippetsCanTBe: Hidden snippets can’t be exported as an image.
imageExportNotices.thatSnippetCouldNotBe: That snippet could not be opened.
imageExportNotices.thatDiagramCouldNotBe: That diagram could not be rendered.
imageExportNotices.couldNotTakeAPicture2: Could not take a picture of this snippet.

shareNotices.nothingToShareYetLoad: Nothing to share yet — load two files or paste some text first.
shareNotices.thatIsNotAUsable: That is not a usable email address — it was not saved. Check for a stray space or comma.
shareNotices.thatDiffCouldNotBe: That diff could not be read — nothing was sealed.
shareNotices.thatFileIsNotA: That file is not a valid public key.
shareNotices.thatFileIsNotA2: That file is not a valid Diff Bro public key.
shareNotices.keyEmailOpened: Your mail app is opening — the key file is on the clipboard, paste it into the message.
shareNotices.keyEmailNoMailApp: No mail app answered. The key file is on the clipboard and revealed — attach it to a message yourself.
shareNotices.thatsYourOwnKey: That's your own public key — you don't need to trust yourself.

compare.summary: open one or two files in a comparison tab
compare.detail:
Opens the files in the running Diff Bro, or starts it first.

One file fills the left side and waits for the right; two open a full
comparison. Paths are resolved against the directory you run this in.

Comparisons open in a new tab, never over the one on screen. With every
tab in use, Diff Bro says so and opens nothing — close a tab and repeat.

difftool.summary: open a comparison git handed over
difftool.detail:
What `git difftool` and `git mergetool` run. Same as compare,
except the two files are known to be throwaway copies git made.

Because they are throwaway, a merge with more conflicts than there are
tabs reuses the oldest of them instead of running out — `git mergetool`
walks the whole conflict list without waiting for anyone.

open.summary: raise the app, optionally on a file
open.detail:
Brings Diff Bro to the front, starting it if it is not running.

With a file, that file fills the left side and waits for the right — the
same as `compare` with one path, under a name that reads like opening.
For two files at once, use `compare`.

backup.detail:
Backs up your snippets, saved diffs, settings and sharing
identity to a zip file at the path you name.

Diff Bro asks for a passphrase first — the archive is encrypted with it,
which is what makes the backup restorable on another machine. Lose the
passphrase and the archive cannot be opened. Restore it from
Security → Configuration → Restore.

create.summary: open a new snippet, or write one at the prompt
create.detail:
Raises the main window with an empty snippet in the editor — the full one, with the name field, syntax picker and tags.

With --interactive (or -i) it asks instead, in the terminal: a name, a syntax and the body, then saves the snippet tagged "cli" so it is findable as one afterwards. An unnamed one is named after the time it was made. At the name prompt, Tab completes against the snippets you already have.

The body takes as many lines as you like. :wq or :x writes it, :q or :a discards it, and Ctrl+C cancels — vim's own meanings, and a line that merely contains one of them is kept as content. An empty body is asked for again rather than throwing away the name and syntax you already gave.

Options: --name takes a name, --syntax takes a name from the list, and --tag may be repeated. A question a flag has answered is not asked.

Pipe a file in and nothing is asked at all: the whole of stdin becomes the body. The prompts go to stderr, so redirecting stdout captures only the confirmation.

help.summary: list the commands, or explain one
help.detail: Prints this list. With a command name, explains that command.

clipboard.summary: save the clipboard as a snippet
clipboard.detail:
Saves whatever is on the clipboard as a snippet named
after the date and time it was saved, guesses the syntax from the content, and
opens it in the editor so it can be renamed or tagged.

An empty clipboard saves nothing and says so.
